clue.text: Concealed acquisition

parts.note: the idiom for something bought sight unseen, so its true nature stays hidden until after the purchase

explanation.surface: Something obtained secretly.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom comes from the old trick of selling a 'pig' in a sack (a poke) that turned out to be a cat or nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a purchase made without inspection, its contents concealed in a bag, so the buyer acquires something unseen.

clue.text: Represent quiet non-professional

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
lay means amateur, not belonging to a profession, as in a lay person

explanation.surface: Speak up for the soft-spoken amateur.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who plays a character represents or portrays that role on stage.

clue.text: The French may enter the gallery regardless of religion

indicators.note: may enter tells us the French article goes inside the word for the gallery

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre
les is the French plural word for the

explanation.surface: French visitors may come into the art gallery whatever their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The gallery' sounds like an art museum, but in a theatre 'the gods' is the top balcony, cheapest and closest to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without any belief in a deity lives without regard to religion.

clue.text: Born dunderhead's requirement

parts.note: née, meaning born, introduces a woman's maiden name
the head (first letter) of dunder is D, the clue word read as dunder-head

explanation.surface: What a fool needs from birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'dunderhead' into 'dunder' plus 'head': the head of dunder is its first letter, D. The 's is just the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is something necessary, a want that must be met.

clue.text: Common or very far from common in a tall tree?

indicators.note: in places the upper-class letter inside the name of the tree

parts.note: the poplar is a tall, slender tree
U stands for upper class, the social opposite of common

explanation.surface: Is a lofty tree ordinary or rather posh?
explanation.walkthrough: The same word 'common' serves twice: the definition means widespread, while 'very far from common' gives U, the old label for upper-class speech and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widely liked or widespread is common among people, the sense of general favour.

clue.text: Hold the fort

explanation.surface: Defend the stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the phrase 'hold the fort', but it splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something is to retain it; a castle's strongest inner tower, its last refuge, also carries this name.

clue.text: Called to account for having accepted a lift to work?

parts.note: if you accepted a lift you were driven somewhere by someone else
a task is a piece of work

explanation.surface: Reprimanded for hitching a ride to the office?
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase literally: someone who accepted a lift has been driven ('taken') to their job ('to task').
explanation.definitionFit: Being rebuked or reprimanded means being made to answer for one's faults.

clue.text: Ruined place indeed! It's well-preserved!

indicators.note: ruined means spoiled or wrecked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a crumbling site that is nonetheless in fine condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' rearranges PLACE and INDEED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus rind boiled in sugar syrup keeps for a long time, a confection literally preserved.

clue.text: Spanish holiday area — a lot's closed off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish resort where much of the place is shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges A, LOT'S and CLOSED (with the S of lot's) into the resort's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The sunny coast of southern Spain around Málaga is a famous package-holiday region.

clue.text: After fifty one makes allowances for tears

indicators.note: after tells us the remaining pieces follow the Roman fifty

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an ace is a one in cards or dice
rations are fixed allowances of food or supplies

explanation.surface: Past fifty, a person sets aside fixed portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' wants to mean weeping, but it is the noun for rips or cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuts and rips in flesh are wounds where the skin has been torn.

clue.text: Check out and put money in one opening

parts.note: to invest is to put money into a venture
I is the Roman numeral for one
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: Inspect the place, then fund a new venture.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine or look into something thoroughly is to inquire into it.

clue.text: What sailors may call a house with yard

explanation.surface: Seafarers' word for a home with a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' is a noun here: the cry sailors give to hail another ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional hail used at sea to attract attention from another vessel.

clue.text: A foot and a quarter gives security

parts.note: an animal's foot is a paw
N, north, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Fifteen inches of length provides safety.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface measures a foot and a quarter; really it is an animal's foot plus a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods left at a pawnbroker's are a pledge, held as collateral against a loan.

clue.text: Charge possibly ten with corruption

indicators.note: possibly signals the word ten may be arranged another way

parts.note: rust is corrosion, a form of corruption of metal

explanation.surface: Perhaps ten people are accused of bribery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like an accusation, but here it is the verb meaning to give someone a duty. 'Possibly' rearranges TEN to ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone responsibility for a thing is to commit it to their care.

clue.text: Colour, seeing winger in a state? No, quite the opposite

indicators.note: in proposes one piece going inside another
this reverses the nesting just given, so the bird holds the state rather than going inside it

parts.note: a winger is a bird, here the tit
NC is the abbreviation for North Carolina, a US state

explanation.surface: Colour of a wide player in a state? No, the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as written, 'winger in a state' puts the bird inside the state; 'No, quite the opposite' swaps the roles, so the state sits inside the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint or shade is a hue, the old poetic sense of the word.

clue.text: European man admitting set-back

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: back tells us the word set is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round

explanation.surface: A man from the continent puts up with a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set-back' looks like one noun meaning a misfortune, but the hyphen hides a word plus its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Malta, the Mediterranean island nation, is a European.

clue.text: Add up silver inside, being a wise man

indicators.note: inside places the chemical symbol within the reversed word
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sum is to add
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Total the silver within and you are a sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Add up' looks like one phrase meaning total, but splits: 'Add' is SUM and 'up' turns it to MUS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Magi, the learned men from the East in the Nativity story, was a sage or sorcerer.

clue.text: Gentleman penning a word of thanks for an instrument

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: sir is the title for a gentleman
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A gentleman writes a thank-you note in exchange for an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' looks like writing, but here it means enclosing, as in a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-necked plucked lute from India is a stringed musical instrument.

clue.text: Putting a note in as well will give trouble

indicators.note: in tells us the musical note goes inside the other word

parts.note: too means as well
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Writing a note too will cause a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or commotion is a bother, a big palaver.

clue.text: Some role!

explanation.surface: What a small acting job!
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is some of a whole; an actor's assigned character is also called by this word.

clue.text: Insignificant growth

explanation.surface: A minor bit of undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means stunted or of little account; as a noun it means low stunted bushes and undergrowth.

clue.text: Confoundedly tried, so rushed out

indicators.note: confoundedly means in a muddled way, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Having made a frustrating attempt, someone dashed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops who made a sally from a besieged position charged out to attack.

clue.text: Official causing trouble in strike

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: biff is slang for hit or strike
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A functionary stirs up trouble during an industrial strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it is BIFF, slang for a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: A court officer who serves writs and seizes goods is a law-enforcement functionary.

clue.text: Palm it — a plot to confuse

indicators.note: to confuse means to jumble, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hide it away: a scheme designed to mislead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm it' reads as sleight of hand, but 'Palm' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The talipot is a tall fan palm of southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Getting rid of the coarse stuff

explanation.surface: Discarding rough material.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissing someone from a job is firing; coarse fabric woven from hemp or jute for bags is also called this.

clue.text: Quit or stay?

explanation.surface: Should I leave or remain?
explanation.definitionFit: To cease is to halt an action; a short visit or halt on a journey is also this.

clue.text: Type of sanctimonious accountant

parts.note: pi is informal short for pious, meaning sanctimonious
CA stands for chartered accountant

explanation.surface: The sort of self-righteous bookkeeper you would avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like 'sort', but it is printing type: pica is a size of typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Pica is a size of typewriter or printing font, twelve points.

clue.text: Green material

explanation.surface: Eco-friendly fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of mown grass is a green; a fine linen or cotton cloth also bears this name.

clue.text: Fly in to sign a treaty

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Travel by air in order to put a name to an international agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' reads as a verb, flying in to sign, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A small two-winged biting insect is a kind of fly.

clue.text: Some beasts celebrated their elevation

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevation means the word is raised up, read from bottom to top

parts.note: sung means celebrated, praised in song

explanation.surface: Certain animals were honoured for their high standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildebeest, the African antelopes, are animals, beasts of the plains.

clue.text: Shortcomings the trainee copies

parts.note: L stands for learner, a trainee driver
imitations are copies

explanation.surface: The novice's faults lie in mimicking others.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaknesses or failings are restrictions on what one can do.

clue.text: Strict stand had RAF all at sixes and sevens

indicators.note: this idiom means in total confusion, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rigid position left the air force in total disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule fixed and unbending, allowing no exceptions, is rigid or strict.
